# Sidebar {.sidebar}

This optional extension sketches a no-server dashboard using a CSV snapshot and Observable JS. It is advanced material for students who want to compare a static dashboard pattern with the Shiny app.

```{ojs}
nhanes = FileAttachment("../../examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv").csv({typed: true})
incomeGroups = Array.from(new Set(nhanes.map(d => d.IncomeGroup).filter(d => d))).sort()
viewof selectedIncome = Inputs.select(["All"].concat(incomeGroups), {
  label: "Income group",
  value: "All"
})
```

# Row

## Mean BMI Across Cycle

```{ojs}
filtered = selectedIncome === "All"
  ? nhanes
  : nhanes.filter(d => d.IncomeGroup === selectedIncome)

adultRows = filtered.filter(d =>
  d.BMI != null &&
  d.Age >= 20 &&
  d.Age <= 80 &&
  d.Cycle != null
)

cycleSummary = Array.from(
  d3.rollup(
    adultRows,
    rows => ({
      n: rows.length,
      mean_bmi: d3.mean(rows, d => d.BMI)
    }),
    d => d.Cycle
  ),
  ([Cycle, values]) => ({
    Cycle,
    n: values.n,
    mean_bmi: values.mean_bmi
  })
).sort((a, b) => d3.ascending(a.Cycle, b.Cycle))

Plot.plot({
  height: 360,
  marginBottom: 70,
  y: {label: "Mean BMI"},
  x: {label: "NHANES cycle", tickRotate: -45},
  marks: [
    Plot.lineY(cycleSummary, {x: "Cycle", y: "mean_bmi"}),
    Plot.dot(cycleSummary, {x: "Cycle", y: "mean_bmi", r: 4}),
    Plot.ruleY([0])
  ]
})
```

## Summary Table

```{ojs}
Inputs.table(cycleSummary.map(d => ({
  Cycle: d.Cycle,
  N: d.n,
  "Mean BMI": d.mean_bmi == null ? null : d.mean_bmi.toFixed(1)
})))
```

# Row

## Interpretation Note

This dashboard uses the cached CSV snapshot and runs entirely in the browser. It is descriptive, unweighted, and not a replacement for the Shiny app or a survey-weighted analysis. Use it as a portfolio extension only after the core reproducibility checks are complete.
